notes.meaning: Solomon originally spoke these proverbs, and years later the scribes serving King Hezekiah gathered and copied them down. God used these faithful men to preserve these valuable sayings so future generations could learn how to live wisely. Preserving God's truth serves the whole community of faith.

God shows His greatness in the things He keeps hidden, because His ways are deeper than human minds can grasp. Good rulers, however, show their honor by digging into matters to find the truth and judge fairly. While God knows all things instantly, earthly leaders must work carefully to bring hidden facts to light.

The sky stretches up beyond reach and the depths of the earth cannot be measured, and the inner thoughts of rulers are just as hard for ordinary people to fathom. Wise leaders often keep state plans private and think through problems on a level that others cannot easily see. It is foolish to guess or criticize motives we cannot fully know.

Silver must have all its scum and impurities melted away before a craftsman can shape a pure, beautiful dish. In the same way, a king must clear corrupt and wicked advisors out of his court. When evil counselors are removed, a government can stand firm on justice and truth.

Pushing yourself forward into the spotlight or grabbing the seat meant for leaders is a dangerous kind of pride. It is far better to wait modestly in a lower place and be invited up than to suffer the public shame of being told to step down. True humility spares us deep embarrassment.

Rushing into a courtroom or starting a lawsuit in a fit of temper often leads to disaster. If the other person proves you are mistaken, you will be left confused, disgraced, and forced to pay for your haste. It is always wiser to calm down and examine the facts before taking someone to court.

When you have a disagreement with a neighbor, talk it over directly with them instead of gossiping to everyone else. Revealing private confidences just to win an argument will brand you as untrustworthy in the eyes of others. Once you earn a reputation as a blabber, that bad name is almost impossible to erase.

A wise word spoken at the exact right moment is as beautiful as golden fruit placed in crafted silver baskets. Proper timing and a kind spirit make good advice delightful to receive. Knowing when to speak is just as important as knowing what to say.

A wise correction given to a person who is ready to listen is like a fine golden earring or necklace. It honors both the person giving the advice and the person humble enough to take it. Listening to good correction adds real beauty to a person's life.

In the scorching heat of harvest, a drink cooled with mountain snow brings wonderful relief to exhausted field workers. A reliable messenger who faithfully carries out his mission brings that same deep refreshment to the master who sent him. Doing what you promised brings peace to those who trust you.

Clouds and wind that sweep across the sky without dropping any rain leave thirsty fields disappointed. A person who loudly brags about gifts or help they never actually give causes that same frustration. It is far better to give quietly than to make big promises you never keep.

Patient endurance can win over a stubborn ruler, and a calm, gentle tongue can break through the hardest opposition. Loud anger usually makes people dig in their heels, but quiet words slowly dismantle tough resistance. Gentleness often accomplishes what force never could.

Honey is sweet and good for food, but eating too much of it will upset your stomach and make you vomit. God provides pleasant things in life, but we are called to enjoy them with self-control. Even good things become harmful when indulged without limits.

Dropping in on a friend too often can turn a warm relationship into irritation. Good manners require giving neighbors their personal space so they do not grow tired of your presence. True friendship grows stronger when we respect other people's time and boundaries.

Telling lies about someone in public or in court is as deadly as hitting them with a club, stabbing them with a sword, or shooting them with a sharp arrow. Slander inflicts severe wounds on a person's life, family, and honor. Lying words are violent weapons that cause lasting damage.

Counting on a dishonest person when trouble hits is like trying to chew with a broken tooth or walk on a dislocated foot. The moment you put weight on them, they give out and cause sharp pain. Real peace comes from putting our ultimate trust in God rather than unreliable people.

Pulling away someone's coat on a freezing day or pouring vinegar on baking soda causes shock and sharp fizzing. Singing lighthearted, party songs to someone who is brokenhearted is just as unfitting and insensitive. Grieving people need quiet compassion and shared tears, not forced cheerfulness.

Feeding a hungry enemy and giving water to a thirsty foe is the ancient way of conquering hatred with love. Meeting their physical needs heaps burning coals on their head by stirring up deep shame and leading them to repentance. The Lord takes notice of this mercy and promises to reward it.

differ.view: Some hold that if showing kindness does not lead an enemy to repent, it increases his guilt and heaps God's fiery judgment upon him.
The burning coals picture smelting metals, showing that returning good for evil is meant entirely to soften and melt the enemy's heart into love.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some early church writers interpreted the coals as the stinging pangs of conscience, while others saw them as divine vengeance on persistent foes.

notes.meaning: Just as a rain-bearing north wind sweeps in wet weather, whispering slander behind someone's back produces angry, darkened faces. Spreading rumors stirs up resentment and breaks down trust between people. Slander would quickly stop if listeners refused to entertain it.

Huddling in an open, windy corner of a flat rooftop is better than living in a spacious mansion filled with constant bickering. Constant arguing strips a home of all comfort and joy. Quiet and simple living is far more precious than luxury ruined by strife.

Receiving good news from a distant country brings deep relief, just like a cool drink of water revives a thirsty, weary traveler. After long days of anxious waiting, hearing that loved ones are safe restores the spirit. Hope fulfilled breathes new strength into the heart.

When a righteous person cowers before evil people or compromises their standards, it is like trampling mud into a clean drinking spring. Good people are meant to refresh and protect their communities, so giving in to the wicked pollutes that helpful influence. Backing down from doing right harms many who look up to us.

Gorging on honey turns a sweet treat into sickness, and endlessly fishing for human praise turns honor into personal shame. Demanding admiration from others reveals an empty and boastful heart. We are called to enjoy life's pleasures with self-restraint and let others praise us rather than seeking our own fame.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin Vulgate, this verse is read as a warning that anyone who pries too boldly into the glorious mysteries of God will be crushed by His majesty.

notes.meaning: An ancient city whose defensive walls have crumbled is completely open to enemy attacks and plundering. A person who cannot manage their own temper or desires is just as defenseless, leaving their heart exposed to every temptation. Self-control acts as a protective barrier that keeps a soul safe from ruin.
